assessments.technical_explanation: The matched text is a literal test fixture inside a redaction test. It is a synthetic private-key marker embedded in a test payload to verify that provider-facing request data redacts multi-token secret assignments. It is not a real credential, is not loaded from any key store, and is never transmitted outside the test process. The surrounding assertions confirm the test's purpose is to ensure such markers are stripped from outgoing request data.

observations.title: Scanner false positive on redaction test fixtures
observations.technical_explanation: Both gitleaks findings originate from synthetic private-key markers deliberately placed in test payloads to verify redaction behavior. The test file's assertions confirm the markers are expected to be stripped from provider-facing request data. This is a classic scanner false positive caused by test data resembling a credential pattern.
observations.layman_explanation: The security scanner flagged fake key text that the project intentionally uses in tests to check its own redaction safeguards. There is no real secret involved.
